## Face form of the gravity work (`gravity-work: face`) {#sec-ch06-face}

### Summary

The face form books, in cell $i$, the work the scheme's own $x_1$ mass fluxes do against gravity: each face's flux
carries mass from the face potential to the cell's centre potential. Its derivation is the template of
@eq-ch06-dwork-booked with $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$, written out as @eq-ch06-dwork-face in @sec-ch06-dwork. This section
covers what the code does around it: it forms the work from the total $x_1$ mass flux after the positivity limiter
and sedimentation, and it replaces the cell work the forcing added (@sec-ch06-cell). It is the only form at the pin;
the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is added to it whenever the grid has a form for that work.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Books the $x_1$ gravity work as a potential-energy flux difference across a cell, @eq-ch06-dwork-face.

**Data.** Reads the total $x_1$ mass flux $F$ on the two faces, face and centre potentials; writes the energy row.

**Placement.** Each stage, after the $x_1$ flux is final and after the forcings; replaces the cell work.

**Activation.** `gravity-work: face`, the default and only value, with $g_1\ne0$ and the $x_1$ flux on.

**Guarantee / limits.** $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ closes to round-off on its own; the booked work is second order.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch06-face-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $b_i$ the per-cell term of the conservation sum [J], $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$ the number of roundings in one
$b_i$ and $\eta_i$ its relative rounding error; $W^{\mathrm{face}}_i$ and $W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i$ as in @sec-ch06-cell.

### Derivation

The stage adds the cell work $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ through the forcing (@sec-ch06-cell). The face form replaces it: the
energy row receives

$$
\Delta E_i \leftarrow \Delta E_i + \Delta t\,\big(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i - W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i\big),
$$ {#eq-ch06-face-energy}

as `gravity_energy_correction = face_gravity_work - original_gravity_work` in `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The code forms $W^{\mathrm{face}}$ in one of two
equivalent ways. On a Cartesian grid `gravity_work_from_face_mass`
({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work.hpp gravity_work_from_face_mass >}}) sums, per cell,
$g_1\big[(x_{1,i+1/2}-x_{1,i})A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2}-(x_{1,i-1/2}-x_{1,i})A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2}\big]/V_i$, differencing the
coordinates before any cast to the working precision, so a large origin does not erase a short cell. On the other
grids it forms $\big(\phi_i\Delta_i[AF]-\Delta_i[A\phi F]\big)/V_i$ from one face product $A\phi F$ per face. Both are
@eq-ch06-dwork-face, since $\phi_i-\phi_{i\pm1/2}=g_1(x_{1,i\pm1/2}-x_{1,i})$.

The face form conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ exactly on a closed column, in four steps:

1. The work is formed from one face mass product per face, read by both neighbours.
2. The density changes by $V_i\dot\rho_i=-\Delta_i[AF]$, so $V_i(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i+\phi_i\dot\rho_i)=-\Delta_i[A\phi F]$.
3. Summed over the column, $-\sum_i\Delta_i[A\phi F]$ telescopes to the two walls, where $F=0$: zero.
4. The other energy fluxes telescope the same way.

Round-off is the one place this shows. With the computed per-cell terms $\hat b_i=b_i(1+\eta_i)$, $\sum_ib_i=0$
exactly and $\lvert\eta_i\rvert\le N_{\mathrm{rd}}\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$, a column of $n_1$[^rg-bf06c25d4aa7] cells and the five
roundings of the stage combination of each $E_i$ give

$$
\Big\lvert\sum_i\hat b_i\Big\rvert \le (N_{\mathrm{rd}}+n_1)\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_i\lvert b_i\rvert
+ 5\cdot\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_iV_i\lvert E_i\rvert \quad\text{per stage},
$$

an upper count, not a measurement. `cellface_check.py` `[C1]` measures the work identity alone,
$\lvert\sum_iV_i(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i+\phi_i\dot\rho_i)\rvert$ over $\sum_iV_i\lvert W^{\mathrm{face}}_i\rvert$, at
$3.9\times10^{-15}$ on Cartesian and spherical-polar columns. Against the exact cell average of $g_1m_1$, with exact
point fluxes, the face form is second order in interior and wall cells (`[C3]`, order 2.00 at $n_1$ = 128 to
256).[^ch06-face-chk] The $O(h^2)$ error is the trapezoid term $\tfrac{h^2}{12}\partial_1^2F$, plus two $O(h^2/r)$
curvature terms on radial grids; the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork removes it in every cell.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch06-face-stencil shows what the face form reads: the two $x_1$ face fluxes of cell $i$ after the positivity
limiter and sedimentation, and the face and centre potentials. The flux is the total mass flux, the dry row plus
every mass-carrying species row (`vertical_mass_flux1`). The block runs when $g_1\ne0$ and the $x_1$ flux is on,
once per stage. With an implicit scheme the correction is added to the right-hand side before the solve, so the
energy the solve inverts is the face-form energy, and the solve's energy row carries the face work of the mass it
moves (@sec-ch06-vic); otherwise it is added after the forcings. @fig-ch06-face-order shows the measured order.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "What the face form reads for cell i: the potential flux phi F at its two x1 faces (orange triangles) and the centre potential phi_i (sky-blue dot), weighted by the distances from the centre to each face."
#| fig-alt: "Three cells with face markers and a centre marker, and the two face fluxes labelled."
#| echo: false
```

### Code

**A minimal input.** `face` is the default, so the gravity block alone selects it:

```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8          # m s^-2; gravity-work: face is the default and only value
```

On a Cartesian, spherical-polar or cubed-sphere grid the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is then booked too;
there is no switch that books the plain face form alone on those grids.

**What is refused, and why.** Any other `gravity-work` value, and the fixer (@sec-ch06-cell, @sec-ch06-fixer).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch06-face-energy** ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
    if (pmb->pcoord->options->type() == "cartesian") {
      auto face_mass = area1.narrow(-1, 0, vertical_mass_flux1.size(-1)) *
                       vertical_mass_flux1;
      face_gravity_work = dt * gravity_work_from_face_mass(
                                   face_mass, pmb->pcoord->x1f,
                                   pmb->pcoord->x1v, volume, is, ie, grav1);
    } else {
    ...
      face_gravity_work = dt * (phi_cell.slice(0, is, ie) * vertical_mass_div -
                                potential_flux_div);
    }
    ...
    gravity_energy_correction = face_gravity_work - original_gravity_work;
```

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| total mass flux, face work, replacement | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `face_gravity_work` | `gravity-work` |
| Cartesian face work | {{< code src/hydro/gravity_work.hpp gravity_work_from_face_mass >}} | `gravity_work_from_face_mass` | none |
| face-area difference | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_face_difference >}} | `x1_face_difference` | none |

: Code map of the face form. {#tbl-ch06-face-code}

1. Sum the total $x_1$ mass flux over the dry and species rows as `vertical_mass_flux1`.
2. Form the face work, Cartesian by `gravity_work_from_face_mass`, otherwise by the two divergences.
3. Add the corrected-PE work where the grid has a form for it (@sec-ch06-dwork).
4. Subtract the cell work and add the result to the energy row, before the implicit solve when there is one.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The plain face work is $O(h^2)$ in every cell; on Cartesian, spherical-polar and cubed-sphere grids the
  corrected-PE work raises it to $O(h^4)$ (@sec-ch06-dwork). On a grid with no $x_1$ measure (`cylindrical`), the
  face form stays second order and setup warns.
- The order above uses exact point fluxes; with the scheme's own fluxes the reconstruction and Riemann errors add.
:::

Combinations with the study switches: @sec-ch12-matrix.
